articles.title: Pill that mimics Viagra can slow Alzheimer’s progression, study suggests
articles.description: Experts call trial results of medication that slowed cognitive decline by almost a third ‘very promising’ A pill that mimics Viagra by relaxing blood vessels and increasing blood flow to the brain can slow cognitive decline in people with Alzheimer’s disease by almost a third, a global study suggests. Alzheimer’s is the most common form of dementia, a condition that is forecast to affect 153 million people worldwide by 2050. There is currently no cure. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Human’ wins Cambridge dictionary’s word of the year
articles.description: Meaning and use of word has become more important in age of AI chatbot, says dictionary In a world where the line between people and machines is more blurred than ever, Cambridge dictionary has sided with natural intelligence for its word of the year: human. Breakthroughs in artificial intelligence – led by the arrival of ChatGPT three years ago – have made the question of what it means to be human as vexed as ever, but the dictionary has drawn a firm line with its choice of the word of 2026, defining “human” as “having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines”.
